summary: When lawyers in different firms may split a fee, and what a lawyer may pay for a referral, in every US state and DC. Each record gives the state's fee-division rule (ABA Model Rule 1.5(e) or its equivalent: the proportion or joint-responsibility test, how the client must agree, whether each share is disclosed, any cap) and its rule on paying for recommendations (Model Rule 7.2(b) or its equivalent: referral-service charges, reciprocal referral agreements, nominal gifts), each quoted from the official rules text with the date read. Cells we could not read at an official source are blank and marked U.

records.text: Lawyers in different firms may split a fee in proportion to each firm's contribution, or if each firm takes joint responsibility for the representation under a written agreement with the client.
records.consentText: The client must agree to each firm's participation, including the share each firm receives, and that participation must be confirmed to the client in writing.
records.feeConditions: The rule speaks of 'firms' rather than 'lawyers'; the total fee must be reasonable.
records.referralServices: A lawyer may pay the usual charges of a legal service plan or a not-for-profit or qualified lawyer referral service (qualified means approved by an appropriate regulatory authority).
records.payDifferences: Alaska has no nominal-gift exception; otherwise the list (ad costs, referral services, practice purchase, non-exclusive reciprocal referrals with client notice) matches ABA 7.2(b).

records.text: Lawyers in different firms, including a referring lawyer, may split a fee if the split is in proportion to the work each does, or each takes joint responsibility under a written agreement with the client, or (in a contingency case) the split is between the referring lawyer and the receiving lawyer.
records.consentText: The client must be told of every participating lawyer and that a fee division will occur, and must not object; the rule does not require a writing.
records.feeConditions: Alabama's third option lets a referring lawyer share in a contingency fee without proportional work or joint responsibility. The total fee must not be 'clearly excessive' (not the ABA 'reasonable' wording). The joint-responsibility option needs a written agreement with the client.
records.referralServices: A lawyer may pay the usual charges of a not-for-profit lawyer-referral service or a not-for-profit legal-aid agency or entity the Office of General Counsel recognizes as legitimate.
records.payDifferences: Alabama's list has no legal-service-plan or practice-purchase (Rule 1.17) item, limits referral services to not-for-profit ones, adds a sponsorship/charitable-contribution item, and bars paying another firm's ad costs unless the two firms jointly represent clients in that matter.

records.text: Lawyers in different firms may split a fee if they sign a written agreement to divide it, the client consents in writing after full written disclosure, and the division does not raise the total fee; there is no proportion or joint-responsibility test.
records.consentText: The client must consent in writing, when the lawyers agree to divide the fee or as soon after as reasonably practicable, after full written disclosure that fees will be divided, who the lawyers or firms are, and the terms of the division.
records.feeConditions: The lawyers need their own written agreement to divide the fee, and the total fee must not be increased solely because of the division. The rule does not apply to a division under a court order (1.5.1(b)). Rule 5.4(a)(4) separately lets a lawyer pay a referral fee to a lawyer referral service operated under the State Bar's Minimum Standards.
records.referralServices: A lawyer may pay the usual charges of a legal services plan or a qualified lawyer referral service, meaning one operated under the State Bar of California's Minimum Standards for a Lawyer Referral Service.
records.payDifferences: California bars compensating, promising or giving anything of value to secure a recommendation, and its gift exception covers any gift or gratuity after a recommendation led to hiring (no 'nominal' limit) as long as it was not promised or understood in advance.

records.text: Lawyers in different firms may split a fee, if the total is reasonable, in one of three ways: by services performed (with the client told and not objecting), under a separation or retirement agreement between former colleagues, or on a referral where each lawyer takes the same responsibility as a partner.
records.consentText: It depends on the route: for a split by services, the client must be advised of and not object to all the lawyers; for a referral, the client must be told the terms and share and consent in a writing the client signs.
records.feeConditions: On the services route the client must also be told if the overall fee will rise; on the referral route the client must be told whether the overall fee will increase. The share is disclosed only on the referral route, so shareDisclosed is null.
records.referralServices: A lawyer may pay the usual charges of a legal service plan or a not-for-profit or qualified lawyer referral service approved by an appropriate regulatory authority.
records.payDifferences: Adds safeguards to the reciprocal exception (client informed consent, no interference with independent judgment, client information protected) and has no nominal-gift exception.
